<!--
  PMS 1.43.4 GET /library/metadata/{showRatingKey}/allLeaves — every episode of ONE show, with the
  reading account's own watch state. Recorded 2026-09-05 from a real server (plex-safety rule 11).
  Titles/ids are the server's own; nested <Media>/<Part>/<Image>/<Role> children are TRIMMED for
  size, and so are episodes 5-8. Container and <Video> attribute names, and the presence/absence of
  each, are verbatim. The real response read `size="8" totalSize="8"`; both are set to 4 below so the
  container describes what it actually carries — a fixture whose own totals disagree with its rows
  makes every paging test lie.

  WHY THIS FIXTURE EXISTS — the stale "finished" date on issue #108. Marking a partly-watched series
  as fully watched bumps the show's `viewedLeafCount` and leaves the show's own `lastViewedAt`
  untouched, so a series finished today still reads as finished months ago. The episodes are the only
  place the real date exists, and this is the read that gets it.

  Two behaviours recorded here that the code depends on, both measured the same day:

  1. `?unwatched=0` IS SILENTLY IGNORED on this endpoint. Filtered and unfiltered both returned the
     same 8 rows. Same failure mode as the section endpoint (see pms_watched_shows.xml.txt) — the
     filter is not refused, it is answered with everything — so `viewCount` is applied client-side.

  2. `totalSize` is ABSENT unless an explicit `X-Plex-Container-Size` is sent. One Piece answered
     `size="1175"` with no `totalSize` and a 3.6MB body unpaged, then `size="50" totalSize="1175"`
     when a container size was asked for. So the page headers are always sent: without them a long
     show is one enormous response AND the walk has no reported total to prove it finished.

  THE TRAP, and why `viewCount` is the filter rather than `lastViewedAt`: episode 2 below carries
  `lastViewedAt="1637560154"` and NO `viewCount` — it has a `viewOffset`, i.e. it was started and
  abandoned. It is NOT counted in the show's `viewedLeafCount`. Dating a show from `max(lastViewedAt)`
  across all episodes would therefore date it from an episode nobody finished, and in this very row
  that abandoned episode is NEWER than the one actually watched (1637560154 > 1637199585) — so the
  naive read is wrong on the first real show it was tried against.
-->
